name: Financial Services v2.0 - Institutional Grade
analyst_brief: The sector spans banks, NBFCs/MFIs, AMCs and insurers. Banks gather low-cost CASA and wholesale deposits and deploy into retail/MSME/corporate credit; asset managers and insurers earn asset-light annuity fees as household savings shift from physical assets (gold, real estate) into financial instruments. Tailwinds include credit growth outpacing nominal GDP, historically low systemic gross NPAs post asset-quality reviews, and India-Stack-driven formalization (Aadhaar, UPI, Account Aggregator). FDI ceilings matter here: private banks and most NBFCs allow up to 74% FDI under the automatic route, while insurance FDI was raised to 74% (from 49%) — this directly caps how much foreign capital can recapitalize a stressed lender or insurer without additional approvals. Headwinds include deposit-mobilization competition compressing NIMs as savers chase term deposits and market instruments, and RBI's periodic risk-weight hikes on unsecured retail/co-lending that tighten funding for lower-rated NBFCs. Moats are built on granular CASA franchises, tier-2/tier-4 branch density, and proprietary underwriting that keeps credit costs low through cycles.
competitive_landscape: Multi-tier oligopoly: large private universal banks capture most incremental profit pool; NBFCs are moderately fragmented, competing on geographic proximity and collateral-specific underwriting.

metrics.indian_nuance: Private banks target 3.8-4.5%; NBFCs/MFIs 7-11%, both sensitive to repo pivots.
CASA>40% is a structural cost-of-funds advantage in rising-rate cycles.
Best Indian private banks sustain <50-80 bps through cycles.
NNPA<1.0% is the institutional 'investible quality' threshold.
Net NPA after provisions is the true asset quality measure.
PCR>70-75% is the PMS filter to avoid future P&L shocks.
Tier-1 banks run 38-45%; branch-expansion phases push this above 50%.
RBI mandates 11.5% minimum; PMS wants Tier-1>14% to self-fund 15%+ growth.
RoA>1.8-2.0% (banks) or >2.5-3.5% (NBFCs) signals superior pricing power.
ROA is the true measure of lending efficiency, stripping leverage.
Mix>25-30% lifts RoA without consuming capital.
Higher promoter skin-in-the-game aligns interests.
Pledging >10% indicates promoter-level stress.
Price to Adjusted Book Value is the standard yardstick for financials.
Strips disguised bad debt hidden in reported book value.
Loan growth must be supported by deposit growth; >500bps gap stresses LCR.
Sustainable profit growth indicates underwriting discipline.
Fresh NPA additions / opening standard advances. Leading indicator of stress before headline GNPA moves.
RBI's early-warning bucket flags latent stress ahead of slippage.
Critical for NBFCs/HFCs; negative short-bucket mismatches caused the IL&FS-style rollover panic.
RBI floor is 100%; PMS prefers >120% buffer in volatile-rate regimes.
Non-par/protection-heavy mix pushes VNB margins to 25-28% for life insurers.
<100% is pure underwriting profit; >100% relies on investment float.
Equity AUM earns 60-80bps yield vs 10-15bps for debt AUM.
Mix>25% raises RBI risk-weight capital charges and default risk in downturns.

red_flags.flag: Large divergence between RBI Asset Quality Review findings and reported NPAs
red_flags.reason: Indicates loan evergreening and can trigger Prompt Corrective Action.

red_flags.flag: Negative ALM mismatch in sub-90-day buckets
red_flags.reason: Exposes NBFCs/HFCs to fatal rollover risk if wholesale funding freezes.

red_flags.flag: Sharp rise in unsecured retail book alongside rising SMA-2
red_flags.reason: Signals growth pursued at the expense of underwriting discipline.

red_flags.flag: FDI headroom near the sectoral cap (74% banks/insurance)
red_flags.reason: Limits the entity's ability to raise emergency foreign capital during stress.
